quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When must you yield to other drivers?

options.text: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
When another car is on your left and you reach an unmarked intersection at the same time.
When your traffic signal is a green arrow.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering a street from a garage or alley.
questions.explanation: You must yield to other drivers when entering a street from an alley, driveway, or garage. You must also yield to pedestrians on an intersecting sidewalk.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but it has a crossbuck sign. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only continue when a flagger tells you it is safe.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When should you always use your signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when pulling into traffic from a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: Your accelerator sticks while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily. Pull off the road when safe and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers in that lane may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose to.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement tells drivers in that lane to make the movement shown by the arrow. Follow any traffic signs or signals before proceeding in the direction indicated.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because of poor visibility. It is difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are traveling. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended if you drive with a blood alcohol level of:

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any trace of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you are not too close to the car you passed. Check your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in the mirror, you have enough room to return safely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.
Pass as safely and quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass as safely and quickly as possible.
questions.explanation: Pass quickly and safely to restore visibility. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane width.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Give the motorcycle only half a lane.
Pass using the same lane as the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane width.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcyclists a complete lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share a lane, the motorcycle needs space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: In fog, should you use high beam headlights to see better?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams in fog. Use low beams or fog lights instead. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow diamond signs warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign means the road will curve sharply to the right, then sharply to the left.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
Drivers should not drive in this lane.
Drivers may use the indicated lane only to make a left turn.
Drivers may drive normally in the indicated lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may drive normally in the indicated lane.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. A green arrow means you can drive normally in that lane.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Reduce your speed.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to hazards. This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead so you can prepare to stop or turn.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep grade ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep grade ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to protect your brakes.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to enter your lane suddenly.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to see you.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to allow room for other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to enter your lane suddenly.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. People may step out without looking, or parked cars may start moving.

questions.question: Which statement is correct about operating your vehicle?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
You should always brake hard to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Brake gently with steady pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop right away. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding with direct pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
There is traffic going both ways on this road.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is traffic going both ways on this road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, you:

options.text: Should move into the lane the arrow points to.
Should slow down and stop if it is safe.
Can turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any cars and pedestrians already in the intersection.
Can drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can turn in the direction of the arrow. First, yield to any cars and pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Always let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in fog.
Looking only straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every 2 to 5 seconds to stay aware of hazards. Looking only straight ahead is dangerous. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road you are on ends ahead.
You must turn either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must turn either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a Y intersection ahead. You must bear right or left.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending. If you are turning in that direction, be ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no vehicle can cross the center line to pass, in either direction.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back into the right lane. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection with no oncoming traffic.
Only where signs and road markings allow passing.
On a curve with no oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only where signs and road markings allow passing.
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections, parking lots, or alleys. Never pass on curves or hills where you cannot see oncoming traffic. Only pass where signs and markings allow it and you have enough safe space.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Frustrate drivers about traffic delays.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, drums, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests to warn you and guide you through the area.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
Only watches the vehicle directly ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instruments regularly. These habits keep you focused while driving.

questions.question: To know where traffic is behind you:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead without emergency braking, which could cause a crash with the vehicle behind you.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles, and you need room to stop if the motorcycle brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one taillight.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn is allowed here.
A left turn can be made only after stopping.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn is allowed here.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means left turns are prohibited.

questions.question: This green arrow on a lane control signal means:

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down over a lane means you may use that lane.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should usually:

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than freeway traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can merge in smoothly and safely. Merging traffic must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Even shallow water can hide hazards. Turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam.
Use high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights only in rural areas when other cars are far away. Use low beam headlights when following closely behind another vehicle.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid yellow arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular yellow light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular yellow light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow has the same meaning as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and get ready for a red light.

questions.question: When backing your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.
Put your head out the driver's side window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Turn your head and look through the rear window when backing. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
Drivers may turn in that direction after stopping completely.
Drivers may turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means traffic cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal.

questions.question: How can you help the driver behind you stay at a safe distance?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes in advance. This helps the driver behind you maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: What do drivers need for interstate driving?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
The ability to stay alert at all times.
Both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to be constantly alert and able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: When daylight begins to fade, what lights should you use to help others see you?

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams as daylight fades. Use high beams only in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely into traffic, you must stop even if the sign says to yield.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When you must yield the right-of-way, you must also stop if you cannot merge safely into the traffic.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when warning signals appear. Do not drive around a lowered gate under any circumstances. Warning signals include flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger, or a train's horn.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and/or flashing lights approaches you, what must you do immediately?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or sirens, pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights and fog lights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic will be entering from the right.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:

options.text: A left turn.
An upcoming stop.
A right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: A left turn.
questions.explanation: Bicycles use hand and arm signals to show their intentions. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are involved in a collision.
If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance while driving. You must show it to an officer after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: You do not have to stop for a school bus that is stopped with its red lights flashing if it is on a private road.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights and its stop arm out. This applies on both public and private roads.

questions.question: If another car is in danger of hitting you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Your horn warns other drivers and pedestrians of danger. Use it if another vehicle is about to hit you.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about blind spots is true?

options.text: Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Won't have any effect on your driving.
Won't put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles the risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two-way traffic is ahead.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.
Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden stops. Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots. Release the gas pedal to let your vehicle slow down, then apply steady brake pressure.
